# 2 Baruch Chapter 17 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 17:2 — "desirable" vs. "something to look forward to"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "[as-for] the-future-[age], it-is-long-and-desirable" | Literal; "desirable" for Syriac t'avta |
| LOGOS | "the future age is long and desirable" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "the future age is long and something to look forward to" | "Something to look forward to" is colloquial |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. "Desirable" is the correct rendering of the Syriac adjective meaning pleasing/good/sought-after. PNEUMA's phrase is accurate but too colloquial for the register.

---

## 17:4 — "adversary" vs. "enemy"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-adversary has-had-dominion" | Literal; "adversary" for Syriac b'el-dababa |
| LOGOS | "the adversary has had dominion over us" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "the enemy has been ruling over us" | "Enemy" for "adversary"; "ruling" for "dominion" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. "Adversary" is the technical term for the satan figure in Syriac (b'el-dababa = "master of accusation"). "Enemy" is more general. "Had dominion" is more precise than "ruling" — it captures the juridical authority sense.

---

## 17:4 — "all those who were not of his time"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "all-those-who-were-not-of-his-time" | Literal — temporal reference to post-Adam generations |
| LOGOS | "all those who were not of his time" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "all who came after him" | "All who came after" — temporal direction specified |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. "Those who were not of his time" is a Syriac idiom meaning 'subsequent generations' — those born into the world after Adam's time. PNEUMA's "came after" is simpler but correct; LOGOS preserves the Syriac phrasing.

---

**Total disagreements this chapter: 3**
